definition: A will which is not written, but is declared orally by the testator. Nuncupative wills are not valid in a majority of states. In states that do permit nuncupative wills, the use of such wills are generally limited to specific instances enumerated by statute. For example, in New York, a nuncupative will must be supported by at least two witnesses and is only valid if made by (1) a member of the armed forces of the United States while in actual military or naval service during a war, declared or undeclared, or other armed conflict in which members of the armed forces are engaged; (2) a person who serves with or accompanies an armed force engaged in actual military or naval service during such war or other armed conflict; or (3) a mariner while at sea.
